title: QuasarSignedBias.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The quasar condition permits nonconvex objectives; convexity is not required.

problem_class.label: quasar
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable τ-quasar-convex minimization: a global minimizer xstar satisfies τ(f(x)−f(xstar)) ≤ ⟨∇f(x),x−xstar⟩ for every x, with 0<τ≤1 and ‖x0−xstar‖≤R.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each query x returns the exact value f(x), together with an inexact gradient, in one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuasarSignedBias.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible oracle-answer clause; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: Call k returns ∇f(x)+b(k+1)−b(k). The hidden sequence b is independent of the query and oracle seed, with b(0)=0 and ‖b(k)‖≤B.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: The additive gradient errors are deterministic and need not be unbiased, vanish, or satisfy a pointwise relative-error bound. B≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: temporal_discrepancy
distinctive_assumptions.details: Errors e_k=b(k+1)−b(k) telescope: ‖Σ_{k=0}^{n−1}e_k‖≤B for every n, and ‖Σ_{k=m}^{n−1}e_k‖≤2B. Errors may persist and cancel across calls; no independence or mixing assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. Gradients exist everywhere and satisfy ‖∇f(x)‖≤M, with M>0; Lipschitz continuity of the gradient is not assumed. E, M, B, R≥0, τ, ε>0, and x0 are public, while f, b, and the minimizer are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuasarSignedBias.lean: Params; spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Output one point in E satisfying f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar; no prescribed iterate or averaging requirement.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the fixed budget max{1,⌈R²(M²+2MB)/(τ²ε²)⌉} oracle calls.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/QuasarSignedBias.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence; supplied OracleTemplate.QuasarSignedBias.result budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Quasar-convex minimization is combined with an unusual deterministic, query-independent telescoping gradient-error model with uniformly bounded cumulative discrepancy, exact function values, and an almost-sure guarantee in an arbitrary real Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Quasar-Convex Minimization with Signed Bias

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is bounded by M>0, and it is τ-quasar-convex about a global minimizer x⋆, where τ∈(0,1]. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, where R≥0. The oracle returns the exact function value and a gradient perturbed by successive differences of a fixed vector sequence bounded by B≥0 and starting at zero. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E with f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives E, M, B, R, τ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Bounded gradient). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, with ∥∇f(x)∥≤M,x∈E.

Assumption 2 (Quasar-convexity and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and f is τ-quasar-convex about this minimizer: τ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩,x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Signed-bias oracle). There is a fixed deterministic sequence (bk)k≥0 in E satisfying b0=0,∥bk∥≤Bfor every k≥0. On call k+1, for k≥0, a query at any x∈E returns (f(x),∇f(x)+bk+1−bk).

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

theorems.formulaHtml: max{1,⌈R2⋅(M2+2⋅M⋅B)τ2⋅ε2⌉+}

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, f is everywhere differentiable, ∥∇f(x)∥≤M, and a global minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and τ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩ for every x. Here M,ε>0, B,R≥0, and 0<τ≤1. Call k returns (f(x),∇f(x)+bk+1−bk) for one fixed, query-independent sequence with b0=0 and ∥bk∥≤B. The target is f(x^)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under any seed law; (1) returns the best-valued queried iterate and succeeds for every seed.

Comparison for QuasarSignedBias.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) QuasarSignedBias (Ours) (review) O(1+R2M(M+B)τ2ε2) value-and-corrupted-gradient calls.
(2) (Jin 2020), Thm. 5.1; special case B=0, E=Rd O(1+R2G2τ2ε2) unbiased gradient calls; expected mean gap ≤ε. Deterministically G=M; exact values select the best iterate at the same total order. (1): Matches known rate at B=0. Scope: telescoping bias and Hilbert spaces; the argument for (2) is dimension-free. (1) needs exact values and excludes stochastic gradient noise permitted by (2).
(3) Derived bound, (Karimireddy et al. 2019), App. B.6; convex f, E=Rd O(1+R2M(M+B)ε2) corrupted-subgradient calls; averaged output. Deterministic subgradients bounded by M, residual ∥ek∥≤ηB, e0=0. (1): Scope extends convexity to quasar-convexity. Matches known rate for convex f, τ=1; formalizes the transferred virtual-iterate bound. (1) requires differentiability and exact values; best-iterate selection replaces averaging without improving the guarantee.
(4) EF-SGD (Karimireddy et al. 2019), Thm. III; convex f, E=Rd O(1+R2σ2ε2(1+1−δδ)) stochastic subgradient calls and compressor applications; expected averaged gap ≤ε. Unbiased subgradients; δ-contractive compression. (1): Scope permits nonconvex quasar-convex objectives and bounded telescoping bias without a compressor. No rate improvement established; arbitrary bias and compressor-generated errors are not generally comparable. (1) requires exact values, differentiability, deterministic errors and query-independent cancellation; no concrete application of this exact error model is established.

Abbr: M: gradient bound; B: cumulative-bias bound; R: initial distance bound; τ: quasar parameter; ε: objective accuracy; η: constant step size; ek: error-feedback residual. In (2), E∥g∥2≤G2; in (4), E∥g∥2≤σ2, 0<δ≤1, and ∥C(v)−v∥2≤(1−δ)∥v∥2.

Jin, Jikai. 2020. On the Convergence of First Order Methods for Quasar-Convex Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2010.04937.
Karimireddy, Sai Praneeth, Quentin Rebjock, Sebastian U. Stich, and Martin Jaggi. 2019. “Error Feedback Fixes SignSGD and Other Gradient Compression Schemes.” In Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, edited by Kamalika Chaudhuri and Ruslan Salakhutdinov, vol. 97. Proceedings of Machine Learning Research. PMLR. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/karimireddy19a.html.

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.QuasarSignedBias

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  M : ℝ
  B : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  τ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := ℝ × p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.M ∧ 0 ≤ p.B ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.τ ∧ p.τ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x, ‖gradient f x‖ ≤ p.M) ∧
    (∃ b : ℕ → p.E, b 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ k, ‖b k‖ ≤ p.B) ∧
      ∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = (f x, gradient f x + b (k.length + 1) - b k.length)) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
      ∀ x, p.τ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ⟪gradient f x, x - xstar⟫)
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.QuasarSignedBias
